transcription:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-11-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Anna Blake (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Martin Cruz (Aurora CTO), Laura Kim (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Head of Cloud Ops)

Summary: (auto) Quick scoping to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing and cost model assumptions. Plan to run bench marks and produce per-token cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated options.

[00:00:00] Anna: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm anna from redwood, i'll kick off - samir and i are here to scope the poc and the cost modeling ask.
[00:00:18] Martin: thanks anna. yes we want a concrete cost model and a pilot that shows latency at our typical loads, and we have some security questions too.
[00:00:30] Samir: great, quick agenda - success criteria, workload sizing (qps, token lengths), benchmark plan, timeline, and then action items. feel free to interrupt.
[00:00:45] Laura: sounds good. to set expectations: our production use is a summarization + Q&A pipeline. median prompt length is about 120 tokens, responses avg 280 tokens, but we have long tails up to 2k tokens. peak rps is around 40 rps, sustained 8 rps.
[00:01:10] Priya: budget wise, we have an initial monthly cap of about $20k for the pilot stage, but we can be flexible if the numbers make sense.
[00:01:22] Anna: perfect, that gives us a baseline. for success criteria what are your must-haves? latency p95, cost per request, and correctness thresholds?
[00:01:34] Martin: must-haves: p95 < 250ms for short responses (<512 tokens) - that's important for UI snappiness. cost per completed response under $0.03 avg for now. quality: no regression vs current baseline embeddings+heuristics.
[00:01:52] Samir: okay noted - p95 250ms target, cost target $0.03 per response. just to align, when you say p95 are you measuring end-to-end (incl network) or service-only?
[00:02:05] Priya: end-to-end from our app to response. network to the hosted API is relevant.
[00:02:12] Samir: got it - we'll capture both service-side latency and end-to-end. for cost modeling we typically break it into per-token compute cost + infra overhead + storage for embeddings/cache. we'll produce a per-token estimate under a few scenarios: hosted shared infra, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/vpc.
[00:02:35] Laura: can you explain how batching and kv cache will affect our numbers? we are worried about latency when batching.
[00:02:42] Samir: yes - batching reduces per-token compute cost: with larger batches we amortize kernel overhead, but it increases queueing which hurts p95. Redwood supports continuous batching and latency SLOs - we can tune target batch sizes and max latency limits. KV/prefix caching reduces repeat token generation and can drop effective tokens per request significantly for repeated prompts or system prefixes. in your summarization pipeline, caching of shared system text could save 15-30% tokens in practice.
[00:03:10] Martin: that 15-30% is huge. how realistic is it for our workload? we have repeated system prompts but also dynamic user prompts.
[00:03:19] Samir: with representative traffic your repeat rate looked like ~20-25% in prior customers; we'll verify with your trace. caching helps most when there are long static prefixes - we'll test a synthetic and real trace.
[00:03:30] Anna: i'll add that our cost model spreadsheet will include assumptions for average tokens in/out, cache hit rate scenarios (low/med/high), and batching settings (target batch size, max latency bucket).
[00:03:42] Priya: on dedicated vs hosted - we want to understand break-even points. our ops team prefers dedicated if it's cost effective and gives predictable latency.
[00:03:52] Samir: absolutely. we usually produce a per-token marginal cost for hosted (pay-as-you-go) and a reserved monthly cost for dedicated normalized to tokens/hour based on expected throughput and utilization. the break-even depends on your sustained qps and utilization. we can run math today with the numbers you gave.
[00:04:10] Anna: do you have a target pilot duration? we typically do 3-4 week pilots for bench and validation.
[00:04:16] Martin: 4 weeks is what we had in mind. start with a week of dry-run benchmarks then 3 weeks of validation on a small slice of production.
[00:04:24] Laura: for benchmarks we want p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and failure rates. also mixed workloads with short and long responses.
[00:04:34] Samir: that's the right list. we'll propose two benchmark configs: (A) low-latency config (smaller batch target, more reserved concurrency) (B) cost-optimized config (larger batching, aggressive caching). we'll run each under your trace distribution.
[00:04:47] Priya: network region matters - our users are mostly east us, europe. do you have regions for dedicated?
[00:04:53] Anna: yes hosted covers US-East and EU-West; dedicated we can allocate in region but provisioning lead time is longer. for the pilot we can use hosted in US-East and test cross-region fallbacks.
[00:05:05] Martin: on security - we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration. also question about data retention for logs and traces.
[00:05:16] Samir: we support SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM for private deployments. for hosted we offer customer-managed KMS options for encryption-at-rest. audit logs retention can be configured - i'll include a short security doc pack.
[00:05:32] Anna: action on that - i'll attach our security checklist to the follow-up email.
[00:05:37] Martin: great. let's try a quick back-of-envelope cost calc with your numbers: if our avg in+out tokens is ~400, and you assume $x per 1k tokens on hosted, how does that work?
[00:05:49] Samir: ok quick example - hosted near-term list price (example) $0.06 per 1k tokens for the model family we think is appropriate; that maps to $0.00006 per token. for 400 tokens that's $0.024 per request. with caching hit say 20% effective tokens -> $0.0192. then network and infra adds small overhead; end result close to your $0.03 target in the low-latency config.
[00:06:14] Laura: can you show the math in the spreadsheet so we can vary model price assumptions?
[00:06:19] Anna: yes the spreadsheet we'll send is parametric - change model price, cache hit, batch size, and it recomputes cost per response and monthly spend under different traffic volumes.
[00:06:29] Priya: what's the typical improvement with quantization or using a smaller model variant?
[00:06:33] Samir: quantization can cut compute cost by roughly 2x depending on model and workload, but may affect quality. smaller model variants give lower cost but you need to validate quality; we recommend A/B evals as part of pilot. we'll include quantized variant bench runs.
[00:06:49] Martin: timeline to get concrete numbers?
[00:06:52] Anna: we'll do: day 1-3 finalise benchmarks and collect traces; day 4-7 run hosted benchmarks; week 2 run dedicated sizing and dedicated bench if you want reserved capacity tests; week 3-4 validation. deliver final cost model and recommendations at end of week 4.
[00:07:10] Laura: can the bench include our latency SLO checks end-to-end?
[00:07:14] Samir: yes we'll run synthetic head-to-head and also a small end-to-end test using your app shim to measure network.
[00:07:21] Anna: we'll also include per-route breakdown (generation tokens, embeddings calls, fees) because your pipeline uses both generation and reranking.
[00:07:31] Priya: what about bursty traffic? we see sudden spikes up to 40 rps.
[00:07:36] Samir: Redwood supports autoscale and burst capacity; cost model will include burst buffer assumptions. dedicated reserved capacity can be sized with headroom or paired with burst-on-demand. we'll show tradeoffs.
[00:07:47] Martin: any gotchas on tokenization differences? sometimes different runtime tokenizers change token counts between models.
[00:07:55] Samir: yes tokenization variance matters - we'll tokenize your corpus against candidate model families and include tokenization overhead in the spreadsheet.
[00:08:03] Laura: for the benchmarks please include a scenario with high long-form responses (2k tokens) because we have occasional long runs.
[00:08:09] Anna: noted - we'll include short/medium/long buckets and weighted distribution.
[00:08:14] Martin: are there sample artifacts we need to share?
[00:08:17] Priya: we'll share a 24h trace, typical payloads, and a list of high-sensitivity fields to redact.
[00:08:23] Laura: we'll upload them to the shared link.
[00:08:26] Anna: perfect. i'll send the shared spreadsheet link and the security checklist.
[00:08:31] Samir: quick note on metrics we will produce: tokens per second, tokens per GPU-hour, p50/p95 latency, percent of requests within SLO, cost per 1k tokens, and effective cost per user request under different cache hit rates.
[00:08:46] Martin: good. i also want to see a sensitivity table: how cost changes with cache hit 0,10,25,50%.
[00:08:53] Samir: yes we'll include a sensitivity analysis and a break-even chart for hosted vs dedicated at different sustained qps.
[00:09:01] (minute markers jump, conversation continues with clarifications)
[00:20:12] Laura: small clarification - when you say dedicated reserved capacity normalized to tokens/hour, does that assume 80% utilization?
[00:20:19] Samir: we usually model 60-80% utilization bands; we'll present multiple scenarios. 80% gives lower unit cost but needs steady load.
[00:20:28] Priya: provisioning lead time for dedicated hardware?
[00:20:31] Anna: typically 2-4 weeks depending on region and availability. we'll plan hosted bench first while dedicated is provisioned if you want dedicated testing.
[00:20:40] Martin: any compliance differences between hosted and private/vpc?
[00:20:44] Samir: private/vpc gives you customer-managed networking and often the KMS is customer-controlled; it's preferred for regulated data. hosted still supports several enterprise controls but has more shared infra constraints.
[00:20:57] Anna: ok as we're closing - recap of next steps: we'll send the spreadsheet, security docs, Samir will share a benchmark plan, aurora to share traces, and we'll target the bench week of 2026-11-22.
[00:21:10] Martin: sounds good. thanks team.
[00:21:14] Priya: quick question - pricing for sustained reserved capacity, is it a monthly commitment?
[00:21:19] Anna: yes dedicated is typically monthly or annual reserved with a commitment; we'll put example numbers in the spreadsheet.
[00:21:25] Laura: can we get a sample SLA for latency?
[00:21:28] Samir: we'll include typical p95 latency SLOs per config and fallback policies.
[00:21:33] Anna: action items and we'll follow up via email with links. thanks everyone.
[00:21:37] Martin: thanks.
[00:45:30] (call ended)

References / Links mentioned: Shared cost spreadsheet link (to be attached), security checklist (to be attached), benchmark plan doc (Samir to share).
